articles.title: Epigenetic changes can be inherited without changing DNA in animals
articles.desc: Typically, the information encoded in DNA allows organisms to develop, function, and pass traits across generations. articles.title: First nonrepeating biological clock discovered in C. elegans guides growth
articles.desc: Imagine a train parked at the station. Passengers climb aboard and find their seats. Conductors move up and down the aisles, checking tickets. But there's a problem—the engineer's watch is broken. As a result, the doors never close, the whistle never sounds, and the train never starts. Something similar occurs in cells when developmental timing is disrupted. Rather than making people late for work, it can mean the difference between maturing into a healthy adult and never growing up at all.
